sentences.text: Tatenectes is a small genus of cryptoclidid plesiosaur, a group of marine reptiles characterized by their distinct body shapes.
This animal possessed a flattened, boxy torso and unusually large belly ribs that exhibited pachyostosis, a condition where the outer layer of bone thickens to increase size and density.
Its skeleton included sixteen dorsal vertebrae, four sacral vertebrae, and a wrist composed of six carpals.
Tatenectes displays an unprecedented condition where osteoporotic bone layers separate its pachyostotic gastralia, despite the animal lacking osteosclerosis.
Evidence from stomach contents reveals that this predator consumed coleoid cephalopods, identifiable by hooklets, as well as hybodont sharks.
Researchers estimated the total length of this creature to be around 2 meters.
The genus Tatenectes was formally established by O'Keefe and Wahl in 2003, with the type species Tatenectes laramiensis named in the same year.
Originally, an incomplete plesiosaur skeleton was described by Knight in 1900 under the name Cimoliosaurus, which is now considered a synonym for Tatenectes laramiensis.
Later, O'Keefe and Street assigned additional material to the species in 2009.
Researchers suggest that the animal's unusual body shape and pachyostotic gastralia helped make it stable and resistant to turbulence near the water's surface.
Stomach contents indicate that Tatenectes fed on cephalopods and fish, specifically targeting coleoid cephalopods and hybodont sharks.
The environment in which it lived was the Sundance Sea, a shallow epicontinental sea where most waters were less than 40 meters deep.
Tatenectes is related to the genus Kimmerosaurus and is classified as a member of the family Cryptoclididae, closely related to Cryptoclidus.
While Tatenectes belongs to Cryptoclididae, its former relatives Aristonectes and Kaiwhekea are now considered derived elasmosaurids.

The taxonomic placement of Tatenectes has varied over time, with some sources classifying it within the family Aristonectidae or Cryptoclididae, though the parent group remains the family Cryptoclididae.
Fossils of Tatenectes have been found in the Upper Jurassic of Wyoming, United States, specifically within the Redwater Shale Member of the Sundance Formation.
Tatenectes lived during the Oxfordian stage, between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago.
The taxonomic placement of Tatenectes and its relatives has varied over time, reflecting ongoing discussions within the scientific community regarding their classification.
